lines.text: Millions of people order French fries every day. But are they actually French?
The potato came from the Andes. Spanish ships carried it to Europe, where people called it pig food... or poison.
Belgium says its villagers fried potatoes first, back in the sixteen-eighties. Lovely story. Except potatoes hadn't reached their valley yet.
France has the stronger case. In seventeen seventy-two, Paris doctors declared the potato safe to eat, and street vendors on the Pont Neuf started frying them.
Thomas Jefferson tasted them in Paris. In eighteen-oh-two, his White House served potatoes, in the French manner.
French fried potatoes were in print by eighteen fifty-six, long before the famous story about soldiers in World War One.
Then came frozen fries, fast food, and the whole planet.
In two thousand three, Congress renamed them freedom fries. It didn't catch on.
So, are they French? Paris made them famous. Belgium made them a religion. And English gave them the name.
